semantic_correction.stem: A client is prescribed subcutaneous NovoLog (insulin aspart) with meals. Which statement by the client shows correct understanding of administration timing?

options.A: I should inject NovoLog within 5 to 10 minutes before starting the meal so the rapid-acting dose is coordinated with the food I am about to eat.
options.B: I should inject NovoLog about 30 to 60 minutes before starting the meal, using the longer lead time associated with slower mealtime insulin.
options.C: I should inject NovoLog after finishing the meal and wait about 30 minutes so I can confirm how much food I consumed before giving the dose.
options.D: I should inject NovoLog at the same fixed clock time each day regardless of when the meal begins because its action is not linked to meal timing.

semantic_correction.rationale: Current U.S. NovoLog prescribing information directs subcutaneous NovoLog to be injected within 5 to 10 minutes before a meal. Therefore A is correct. B uses a substantially longer premeal interval that is not the labeled timing for NovoLog. C delays the dose until after the meal rather than using the labeled premeal interval. D incorrectly treats NovoLog as a fixed-clock medication independent of meal timing. The item is deliberately product-specific and does not generalize NovoLog timing to every insulin-aspart formulation or every mealtime insulin.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Teach clients using subcutaneous NovoLog to administer it within 5 to 10 minutes before a meal and to follow product-specific insulin instructions rather than generalizing timing across mealtime insulin products.
semantic_correction.source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine DailyMed / U.S. Food and Drug Administration labeling
semantic_correction.source_version_date: DailyMed page updated December 9, 2023; prescribing information revised December 2023; live label rechecked August 20, 2026
semantic_correction.source_locator: Section 2.2 Preparation and Administration Instructions for the Approved Routes of Administration — Subcutaneous Injection: inject NOVOLOG subcutaneously within 5 to 10 minutes before a meal. Highlights repeat the same 5–10 minute premeal timing.
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: Subcutaneous NovoLog is labeled for injection within 5 to 10 minutes before a meal.
semantic_correction.blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
semantic_correction.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12 (official PDF pageno 15): prepare and administer medications using rights of medication administration; review pertinent data prior to medication administration; educate client about medications; evaluate client response to medication; handle and administer high-risk medications safely.
semantic_correction.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — product-specific rapid-acting insulin administration timing
semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup retained the NovoLog meal-timing construct, removed the original ‘all’ distractor cue, rebuilt A/B/C/D to parallel statements, and narrowed the tested claim to the current NovoLog label without cross-product timing generalization.

scope_exclusions.dose: No insulin dose, carbohydrate ratio, correction factor, or titration calculation is tested.
scope_exclusions.other_products: The item does not claim that Fiasp, other insulin-aspart products, regular insulin, or other mealtime insulins share NovoLog's timing.
scope_exclusions.route: The stem specifies subcutaneous NovoLog and does not test pump or intravenous administration.
scope_exclusions.missed_dose: No missed-meal or missed-dose protocol is tested.
scope_exclusions.meal_consumption: The item assumes a planned meal and does not address delayed intake, nausea, NPO status, or uncertain food availability.
scope_exclusions.hypoglycemia: Hypoglycemia risk is clinically relevant to insulin but is not the primary construct tested here.

near_duplicate_check.note: Targeted GitHub search for ‘NovoLog 5 to 10 minutes before meal insulin aspart timing’ returned no indexed repository match. No broad bank scan was performed.

option_audit.A: Correct. It matches the labeled 5–10 minute premeal timing for subcutaneous NovoLog.
option_audit.B: Plausible because longer premeal lead times are familiar from other insulin teaching, but this is not the labeled NovoLog interval.
option_audit.C: Plausible because post-meal dosing can be considered with some products or situations, but it is not the labeled routine timing tested for NovoLog.
option_audit.D: Plausible to a learner who confuses mealtime insulin with scheduled basal therapy, but NovoLog dosing is coordinated with meals.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible best answer. A alone matches the product-specific labeled timing. B, C, and D use timing patterns inconsistent with the NovoLog subcutaneous label.

cueing_check.note: All four options are parallel first-person timing statements with comparable length and no all/only/always/never/every cue.

blueprint_audit.entry_level_relevance: Safe medication administration and medication teaching are explicit 2026 NCLEX-RN activities, and insulin administration timing is a high-value entry-level medication-safety construct.
blueprint_audit.visual_verification: VERIFIED. Official 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan screenshot pageno 15 / printed p.12 was successfully retrieved August 20, 2026 and visibly shows the cited Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies activity statements.
